title: Update a register field
description: Implement uint32_t update_field(uint32_t reg, uint32_t mask, uint32_t value).
prompt:
Implement uint32_t update_field(uint32_t reg, uint32_t mask, uint32_t value).
Replace only the bits selected by mask with the corresponding bits from value. value is already shifted to its register position. This operates on a value, not a volatile peripheral address.
constraints: No shifts, heap allocation, or peripheral access are necessary.

tests.name: Replace low nibble
Empty mask
Full mask
Ignore value outside mask

reference_solution.solution.c:
#include <stdint.h>
uint32_t update_field(uint32_t reg, uint32_t mask, uint32_t value) { return (reg & ~mask) | (value & mask); }

rubric: Respect the stated contract and bounds.
Explain integer widths, ownership, and relevant edge cases.
Separate host-test evidence from hardware guarantees.
follow_ups: Why can a read-modify-write be unsafe on a hardware status register?
How would write-one-to-clear bits change this API?
hints: Write down the boundary cases before choosing an implementation.
Use explicit integer widths and keep intermediate values in range.
